Check out @JonLaymonStudios 

Never pour epoxy in a rising temperature environment. Pour on a steady or falling temperature. If the shop is warming while it cures, air in the wood expands and pushes up through your coat. Source: West System User Manual & Product Guide

Room temp 72 to 75°F, humidity under 60 percent. High humidity means cloudiness. Source: Jess Crow (temperature). Humidity guidance is standard across epoxy manufacturers.

Silicone cups and spatulas. Cured epoxy pops right off, no waste, and no wood fibers from stir sticks contaminating the pour. Source: general shop practice

Warm the bottles before mixing. Thinner resin releases bubbles better. BUT.
